body:
## Summary
Build C4 as ONE producer: an explicit, per-share consent flag (stored as a filterable column), a cohort reader that returns anonymous payloads only for consenting members of the org, and a pure aggregate builder that runs the floors that already exist (CHAMPION_MIN_POP, careBandFromSharers) plus a k-floor on kept-move titles. The same aggregate feeds the Contributors Care section and the consenting viewer's own orgBands.

## Description
The care loop has a working personal half (C3) and a fully designed org half (CareOrgView, careBandFromSharers, CareOrgBands, the 'comparison off' ring) with nothing between them: getCareOrgAggregate never reads a share and nothing fills orgBands. It cannot simply start reading MentorShare, because the contract has no consent field and the row is global per login, so any read today would turn 'I stored my notebook' into 'my org reads my numbers' - the exact flow private-view-separation forbids ('nothing computed here flows upward ... it may not become one by being harvested'). The move: consent becomes data the producer filters on, and suppression is enforced in the producer, never at the surface (producer-enforced-suppression: 'withheld values never leave the producer', 'one door').

Pieces: (1) contract gains optional consent:{orgAggregate:boolean}, refused when not boolean, absent = false; (2) MentorShare.orgAggregate Boolean @default(false), written by saveMentorShare from the validated share; (3) src/lib/db/mentor-share-cohort.ts getOrgCareCohort(slug): refuses PUBLIC_ORG, resolves the org's member githubLogins via Membership->User, counts share rows of members (setUp, existence only), and selects payloadJson ONLY where orgAggregate=true - returns {setUp, shares: CareSharePayload[]} with no login; (4) src/lib/org/care-org-aggregate.ts buildCareOrgAggregate(population, cohort): belowFloor short-circuits everything; per shape field, only fields each sharer actually shared (validateCareShapePayload sharedFields) go into careBandFromSharers; topKeptMoves grouped by normalized title and dropped below CARE_KEPT_MOVE_MIN (= CARE_BAND_MIN_SHARERS) because a free-text title kept by one or two people identifies them; asks and outcomes stay honestly empty (no source in the contract); (5) getDeveloperView sets orgBands from the same aggregate only when the viewer's own share consented; (6) one switchable privacy-ledger row 'Anonymous org bands'.

Governing subject: people-analytics-ethics - techniques producer-enforced-suppression, naming-population-floor (small-cell suppression on free-text cells), private-view-separation (consent is the only path upward).

## Flow
- Developer POSTs a share with consent.orgAggregate=true -> column set true
- Contributors Care section -> getCareOrgAggregate(slug) -> getOrgCareCohort(slug) -> buildCareOrgAggregate(population, cohort)
- Below CHAMPION_MIN_POP: suppressed whole; per field below 5 sharers: bandGaps reason; kept titles below 5: dropped
- Developer page: own consent true -> orgBands = aggregate.shapeBands -> CareSessionShape draws the quartile strip with 'your value marked'

## Expected impact
The Contributors Care section and the session-shape comparison stop being permanently empty for any workspace with >= 5 consenting sharers, with no new per-person read reachable by the org, and every existing share stays out by default.

## Evaluation
Claim: the org aggregate is produced from consenting members' shares only, floored in the producer, and feeds the consenting viewer's bands.
Before: 1 of 8 cases pass (case 7 by design)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: contract (share contract + additive column; default-off consent keeps every existing row out)
notes_from_critic: in-scope contract (not policy-loosen): default-false consent, producer-enforced suppression, cohort read returns no login. Use a migration timestamp later than providers-0 and oauth-1.

## Summary
The care loop's only door (POST /api/me/mentor/share) accepts the browser session and nothing else, and the page that holds that session has no way to use it. Add one control in the Setup card: paste or drop a share file, see a preview computed by the server's own validator and ledger (what lights up, what stops being shared, what was refused and why), then commit in one click; plus delete-my-share with a confirm step. Every unwired 'Share again' / 'Share an update' button opens it.

## Description
Today a developer who has a share (hand-written, or produced by the mentor once C2 ships) cannot get it onto their own page without opening devtools and hand-crafting a fetch: the route doc admits the CLI cannot authenticate (#22 is concept-doc first) and the page 'has no upload or delete control of its own'. Meanwhile every share affordance logs to the console. The decision the user makes blind is consent: a POST replaces the snapshot whole, so pushing a share without 'moves' silently stops sharing moves. The app already has every piece needed to show that before it happens: validateCareShare and careShareLedger are pure and run unchanged in the browser.

shareUploadModel.ts (pure) maps input text + the current view to a typed state: empty | invalid | too-large | refused | ready (ledger rows that will light, sections that will stop being shared, counts of moves/journal/shape fields) | saved | signed-out | confirm-delete | nothing-stored. careShareClient.ts wraps POST/DELETE and maps 400/401/404/413/503 onto those states. CareShareUpload.tsx renders a textarea + file drop, the preview on the same MatrixGrid ledger vocabulary, Commit and Delete; disabled whenever view.demo is set so a preview fixture can never be pushed. Governing subjects: people-analytics-ethics private-view-separation ('say so in the product': the person sees exactly what leaves before it leaves) and draft-editing (preview-then-commit of a replace-whole snapshot).

## Flow
- Setup card -> 'Share again' opens the upload panel
- Paste/drop -> preview: refused keys named by path, ledger rows lit, 'you stop sharing: moves, journal'
- Commit -> POST -> refresh -> the page renders the stored share (profile.sharedAt set, preview control disappears)
- Delete -> confirm -> DELETE -> refresh -> honest empty state

## Expected impact
The care loop goes from unreachable without devtools to one paste and one click, with the consent consequence visible before commit, and the 'delete leaves nothing behind' guarantee becomes something a developer can actually exercise.

## Evaluation
Claim: a developer can preview, commit and delete their own share from the page, and the browser refuses exactly what the server refuses.
Before: 0 of 8 cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: none (owner-self route unchanged, no auth or contract change)

## Summary
The three report exports each hand-roll the same preamble (parse, owner-only org, gate, NON-strict read, 404/503, filename) and have drifted from the permalink twice: they ignore the page's ?org hint and they never took the 2026-10-07 strict read. One `readReportForExport` door makes 'export what the page shows' structural.

## Description
`src/lib/report/report-org.ts` takes `resolveReportOrg(owner, hint)` out of page.tsx so the page and the exports resolve the tenant by one rule (canReadOrg-gated hint, else readableOrgForOwner). `src/lib/report/export-read.ts` owns parse -> resolve -> requireOrgRead -> strict getScanReportByCommit -> {404 empty | 503 unavailable} -> filename stem, returning `{ report, orgSlug, parsed, stem }` or a Response. The three routes keep only their own concern (plan gate + render for PDF, markdown for LLM, ImageResponse for the card). `src/lib/report/export-href.ts` builds the export URLs ReportHeader renders and forwards the page's `org` param. A source-scanning guard (comments stripped, seeded violation) pins that no export route reads the report outside the door.

Technique: authorization / dispatch-chokepoint-gating (one door every export passes) and failure-direction (an outage must not degrade toward 'not found').

## Flow
- /report/acme/app?org=rebrand renders the report read under 'rebrand'
- Export PDF / Share card hrefs carry &org=rebrand; the door re-gates it with canReadOrg (never trusted)
- door reads strict under the same org -> same report, same bytes as the chip
- DB outage -> 503 try again, not 'Scan it first'

## Expected impact
Exports can no longer hand back a different (public-org) report than the one on screen, or tell a user to spend a scan during an outage. Never widens reach: the hint is re-checked by canReadOrg and an unreadable hint falls back exactly as today.

## Evaluation
Claim: exports read the same tenant, the same strictness and the same report as the permalink.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass
After: 6 of 6 (plus 3 guards green before and after)
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: contract

## Summary
'Copy for LLM' dumps the whole report, and its endpoint twin takes no options, so an agent tasked with one dimension gets the whole document, and the org's measured lifts (which the roadmap on screen shows) never reach the model. Turn the chip into a small composer: pick dimensions, see the size, copy the text or the equivalent endpoint URL, and both carry the measured clause.

## Description
`src/lib/report/briefing-scope.ts` (pure) owns `parseBriefingScope` (same dims grammar as /api/report/skill, unknown -> error), `scopeReportForBriefing` (narrows dimensions, gaps, evidence, discrepancies and roadmap to the selection; strengths/risks stay, being report-level strings), the honesty lead line (a scoped briefing says it is partial and that the headline score is whole-repo, the scope marker a pasted text otherwise loses) and `briefingHref`. `reportLlmMarkdown` gains one `scopeNote` option; the unscoped output stays byte-identical. The endpoint parses ?dims (400 on unknown) and reads `getOrgExpectedLifts` under the org it already gated; ReportView forwards `serverLifts` to ReportHeader so the chip passes the same map. `BriefingComposer` wraps the existing CopyForLlm with a dimension multiselect, a lines/approx-token readout and 'Copy URL'. Builds on card A's door when both land (the route change is then ~25 lines on the thin route).

Techniques: executive-reporting/provenance-caveats (a partial briefing states its partiality in the body); invariant-placement/completeness-at-emission (the payload the model reads carries every field the page shows).

## Flow
- viewer opens the composer on the report header
- picks D3 + D9 -> preview reads '214 lines, ~3.1k tokens'
- Copy text -> scoped briefing with the scope lead line and measured clauses
- or Copy URL -> /api/report/llm?repo=...&dims=D3,D9 returns the same bytes for a script/agent

## Expected impact
An agent handed one dimension gets a briefing about that dimension, and the roadmap it reads carries the org's own measured outcomes instead of silently omitting them. No new reach: lifts are read under the same gated org as the report; anonymous viewers get EMPTY_LIFTS and today's bytes.

## Evaluation
Claim: the briefing can be scoped, is scoped identically by chip and endpoint, and carries measured lifts.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass
After: 6 of 6 (plus 2 guards green before and after)
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first

## Summary
The webhook route is 837 lines of if/else where the tenant bind (`installationMatchesOwner`) is hand-called by five arms and skipped by three. Turn the arms into one table where an arm that writes tenant state cannot run without a `BoundDelivery`, and close the three skips.

## Description
The route's own doctrine (route.ts:137-142) says a valid HMAC proves a delivery is authentic, not that its (installation, owner) pair is real, so every tenant write must bind first. The push, PR-gate, probe and registry arms do. Three arms don't. (1) Repo-control attribution runs after `enqueueControlProbe` has already refused the owner, because that function returns void on a mismatch (route.ts:323-326, 796-809). So a mismatched delivery still writes an actor-attributed row into the named org's governance ledger. (2) and (3) `pull_request_review` and `pull_request.closed` write AiChange approval and merge evidence for the payload owner with no bind at all (route.ts:735-748, 438-492). That is the conformance pack's evidence population. This is the 'two implementations of one rule where only one was fixed' shape: the bind is a convention (pr-gate.ts:48 makes it optional), not a precondition.

The move: `arms.ts` declares one row per event: preconditions (app, db), `bind: 'owner' | 'github-confirmed' | 'none'`, the declared effects, `extract(payload)` and `run(bound, payload)`. The route does bounds -> verify -> parse -> claim -> `dispatch(event, payload, delivery)`. `dispatch` runs `bindDelivery` once for an owner-bound arm and hands `run` a branded `BoundDelivery {installationId, orgSlug, deliveryId}` it cannot fabricate. The review/merge arms bind on the stored mapping only, so they still mint no token and make no GitHub call (stored mapping only, no live confirm). Signature verification, the bounded read, the dedup claim and the 24h horizon are untouched.

## Flow
- route.ts: readBoundedText -> verifyWebhook -> JSON.parse -> claim (unchanged) -> dispatch
- dispatch: arm = ARMS[event]; unmet precondition -> no-op; bind 'owner' -> bindDelivery or abandonDelivery once and stop
- run(bound, payload): probe + attribution share ONE bound value; AI-change uses bound.orgSlug, not the payload login
- arms.test.ts: data-table guard (no source scanning) + seeded violation + doc-table equality

## Expected impact
No signed-but-misrouted delivery can write a governance attribution or AiChange evidence row into an org whose installation it does not hold (today 3 arms can). The bind becomes structural. A new arm (e.g. deck #21 identity sync) cannot ship without declaring one, and cannot ship undocumented. Applies webhook-ingestion / sender-authentication (one-validation-door) and the identity-survives-reuse law.

## Evaluation
Claim: every tenant-writing webhook arm runs only behind the installation->owner bind
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-3 and 7 fail on today's code; 5-6 have no table to test)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first in owner-bound-arms.test.ts and arms.test.ts, then the relocation, then the two bind closures
Result: better

## Summary
The foundation panel's report-back column shows something false today. Every repo shares one org-wide credential name, so provisioning the second repo revokes the first repo's token. The panel still shows both as Provisioned. Give each repo its own credential and make the row state honest: live / failed / credential revoked / legacy shared. Put the fix on the row itself.

## Description
Today an owner provisions report-back repo by repo through a typed confirmation, and each success notice says that repo 'now reports its conformance back on every CI run'. Every POST rotates the single `conformance report-back` token, and rotation retires every live token of that name (org-api-tokens.ts:163-167). So after provisioning ten repos, only the last one's CI can post a score. The other nine 401 silently. The panel reads its state from audit rows that never check `ok` or token liveness (org-foundation.ts:91-106), so all ten show Provisioned. Revoking one repo kills all of them. A 403 for missing `Secrets: write` also shows as Provisioned. And because rotation runs before the write, the 403 has already revoked that repo's working token.

The owner's next decision, which repos need attention, is made blind. The app already has the data: the audit row's `ok` and `tokenPrefix`, and the OrgApiToken table's live prefixes. This card changes three things. (1) Per-repo credential: `tokenNameFor(fullName)` is a stable name of at most 80 chars, and the hash suffix keeps it unique. (2) Order: mint, write both secrets, then retire this repo's previous token. On a failed write, retire the just-minted one instead. (3) A `reportBack` state on the row, joined from audit meta and live token prefixes. The row then offers the action that fits: Re-provision for a revoked or legacy credential, the App's configure URL for a missing permission. The typed one-repo confirmation and the owner gate stay exactly as they are.

## Flow
- POST secrets: gate (unchanged) -> mint token named tokenNameFor(repo) -> put both secrets -> on success revoke same-name tokens except the new id; on failure revoke the new id
- DELETE: revoke tokenNameFor(repo) only (plus the legacy shared name ONLY when no other repo still reads legacy-shared)
- getFoundationRollout: provisioned row + meta.ok + tokenPrefix in live set -> live / failed(reason) / credential-revoked / legacy-shared
- row view: state word + one action; viz counts only live

## Expected impact
A fleet of N provisioned repos has N working credentials, not 1, and the panel's 'provisioned' count equals the repos that can actually report. A leaked repo secret now exposes one repo's credential, not the whole org's report-back. The Passports capability matrix stops saying 'provisioned - never reported' for a repo that cannot report. Registry: conformance-checking / declared-then-proven, plus the absent-guard-is-loud law.

## Evaluation
Claim: provisioning or revoking one repo's report-back never changes another repo's, and the row shows the credential's real state
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first (route.test.ts, org-foundation.test.ts, reportback-credential.test.ts, foundationViz.test.ts)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten (a credential's reach narrows from org-wide-shared to one repo; no auth gate loosens)

The launch map's Scan button is a third, hand-rolled consumer of POST /api/org/scan. It reads only `repo` frames, so every in-band refusal (out of credits, server failure) and every budget-stopped remainder is reported as 'No watched repos to scan'. Put the map on the transport (useScanStream) and the roster model (scanRunRosterModel) the dashboard button already uses, behind one `useFleetScan` hook and a pure `fleetScanOutcomeModel`.

## Description
The stream contract has five frame kinds (repo, notice, queued, result, error). useOrgScanButton folds all of them through foldStreamFrame/foldQueueSnapshot and renders rosterGroups with one remedy per group. FleetMap.scanOrg tallies `applied`/`inapplicable` integers from repo frames only and falls through to a hard-coded empty-watchlist sentence: two implementations of one rule, and only one was fixed (c2ec4a4e). The move: (1) add an optional `signal` to ScanStreamRun so the map keeps its unmount abort; (2) `useFleetScan(installations)` owns scanning/scanError/scanCtrl/scanGen/recentScan, drives useScanStream, paints stars through the unchanged applyScanEvent, folds a roster per org, follows a `queued` run with startQueueFollow and, when it drains, clears recentScan and pulls that org once; (3) `fleetScanOutcome(roster, inBandError, queued)` is the pure answer to 'what does this card say and offer'; (4) ConstellationField's footer is extracted and renders that outcome (message plus the group's one action: Retry failed / Add credits / Reconnect). - Click Scan -> useFleetScan.scan(login) -> useScanStream({body:{org}, signal}).
- Each frame -> applyScanEvent (stars) + foldStreamFrame (roster); `error` -> inBandError; `queued` -> queue follow.
- Stream end -> fleetScanOutcome -> the footer shows the reason and its remedy; a queued tail keeps ticking until drained, then the org is re-pulled.

No map scan ends on a false sentence: an out-of-credits owner is pointed at /pricing, a token-less one at Integrations, and a partial run gets one-click retry of exactly its failures. The fleet map lets you build a precise question ('unscanned repos', 'L1 across orgs', 'repos named *api*') and then only dims the answer. ## Summary
The nightly purge counts and deletes every aged ledger with two separately written predicates, and carries 15 counters through ~8 hand-written lists. Declare each purged ledger once, in a table, and let the preview, the delete, the result row, the audit meta and the rollup all derive from it. The same move fixes a recorded registry deviation: counts of committed batches are lost when a later batch throws.

## Description
The erase path already got this right with its `drain(find, count, del)` closure (retention.ts:1800). The purge path did not. Its dry run (retention.ts:867) is a second implementation that counts, and the golden path's dry-run-preview technique calls that out as a lie waiting to happen. Today a new ledger such as a wave-5 table has to be edited into about 8 places inside `purgeExpiredData`. If it is missed in the dry-run branch, the preview under-reports. If it is missed in `totalDeleted`, the audit trace is skipped.

- `retention-ledgers.ts`: `PURGE_LEDGERS`, a readonly array of descriptors `{ key, horizon: 'audit', where(orgId, cutoff), orderBy, children?, keepNewestPerPair? }`, plus `sweepLedger(desc, mode: 'count'|'delete', acc)`. The sweep adds into a caller-owned accumulator after every committed batch. The control-observation keep-newest rule and conformance findings-before-report become descriptor fields, not special branches.
- `retention-counters.ts`: `PURGE_COUNTER_KEYS` (const tuple), `zeroOrgResult()`, `sumDeleted(r)` (excludes digestsWritten and scansCompacted, as today), `rollup(results)`, `auditMeta(r)`. There is also a compile-time assertion that the keys equal the numeric keys of `OrgPurgeResult`.
- `pruneRepoScans` takes an accumulator instead of returning locals, so the catch block at :1232 sees real partial counts.
- `purgeExpiredData` becomes a loop over `PURGE_LEDGERS` with one `mode` flag. The budget checks, floor refusal, rotation and orphan/queue/quota sweeps are unchanged.

## Flow
- Resolve the policy, check the floor and compute the cutoff (unchanged).
- Scan prune per repo writes into acc (per batch).
- For each descriptor: sweepLedger(desc, dryRun ? 'count' : 'delete', acc), with a budget check between them.
- On success or throw: results.push(acc), since there is one row builder.
- If sumDeleted(acc) > 0 and this is not a dry run: recordAudit(PURGE_ACTION, auditMeta(acc)).

## Expected impact
The preview equals the delete by construction, not by comment. Adding a ledger is a one-row edit. The registry deviation at :1005 closes. purgeExpiredData drops by roughly 300 lines.

## Evaluation
Claim: preview and delete share one predicate per ledger, and committed counts survive a throw

After: 7 of 7

## Summary
Owners edit a destructive policy and approve it after seeing five numbers. Those numbers are the absolute total, not the effect of the edit, and the card never says whether the purge it promises ever ran. The card should show the full per-ledger blast radius as a delta between the current and proposed policy, and a receipt for the last purge.

## Description
The erase dialog was brought up to the full blast radius in c40708f73. The retention preview was not, and it still hides governance evidence (control observations), the LLM meter (usage events) and conformance history, even though the server already counts them. The decision an owner is making is 'what does tightening 90 to 30 days cost me', and the screen cannot answer it.

- `retentionPreviewModel.ts` (pure): `(baseline: OrgPurgeResult | null, proposed: OrgPurgeResult | null) -> { state: 'ready'|'unknown', groups: [{ title, rows: [{ key, label, now, proposed, delta, unknown }] }] }`. It reuses the BLAST label table from erasePreviewViz.ts, omits counters the body did not carry, and propagates `null` digest counts as unknown.
- Route: when the draft differs from the stored columns, run previewOrgRetention twice (stored, then proposed) and return `{ preview, baseline, errors }`. This replaces the hand-written `emptyPreview` zero list.
- `retention-receipt.ts`: `getRetentionReceipt(slug)` returns the newest `retention.purged` and `retention.updated` rows for that org id only.
- `retentionReceiptModel.ts` (pure) maps those to 'applied' | 'not-since-save' | 'never', with honest copy.
- `RetentionPreviewPanel.tsx` renders the delta table, the errors line and the receipt strip. RetentionCard keeps the form and the fetch.

## Flow
- Settings loads, and the receipt strip reads 'Last purge removed 15 rows on Oct 21 · policy saved Oct 3'.
- The owner edits the audit days and previews.
- A grouped table appears: Governance > Control observations 0 -> 40 (+40); any errors appear in an alert.
- Save stays gated on a successful preview, as today.

## Expected impact
The owner sees the marginal cost of the edit across every ledger before saving. A failed preview can no longer read as 'deletes nothing'. The promise in 'applies on the next nightly purge' gets a visible receipt.

## Evaluation
Claim: the card reports the edit's per-ledger delta, reports unknown as unknown, and shows the last-run receipt
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass
After: 7 of 7

## Summary
The external MCP door hands org- and agent-authored text (memory bodies, skill bodies, LESSONS.md entries, governing subjects) to third-party coding agents with credential shapes intact, while Athena redacts the same results. Declare each tool's result trust in the catalog, apply one pure egress (redactSecrets over string leaves, shape-preserving) at the door, and stamp additive provenance/redaction _meta.

## Description
The redaction rule exists once (untrusted.ts sanitizeAgentText) but is applied at only one of the two doors that serve these handlers, keyed by a hand-list in Athena's file. An external agent's model vendor is a further egress the org did not choose; a token pasted into a lesson travels to it on every get_skill_lessons call. Applies mcp-tools/untrusted-result-handling (data with provenance, never instruction) and prompt-safety/output-sanitization ('deciding which egresses mask and which stay verbatim') + cross-language-rule-parity ('masked on screen but raw in the log'). Backward compatible: result shapes and keys unchanged, content stays JSON text (no fence injected into an external client's parse), _meta keys are namespaced and additive. Narrows, never widens, what a token reads.

## Flow
- tools.ts: McpToolDef.resultTrust: 'computed' | 'org-authored' (required), org-authored on the five tools Athena fences.
- result-egress.ts: egressResult(def, result) -> {result, redactions}; walks structuredContent string leaves and result.text through redactSecrets for org-authored tools; identity for computed.
- route.ts: egress before toolResultText; when org-authored add _meta {'ascent.dev/provenance':'org-authored','ascent.dev/redactions':n}.
- Parity test pins the catalog's org-authored set to ATHENA_UNTRUSTED_TOOLS so the two doors cannot drift (Athena may later derive from the field; grounding.ts is a shared surface, not edited here).

## Expected impact
Zero raw credential shapes leave the agent door; the org can see per-call redaction counts; Athena and MCP stop disagreeing on the same rule.

## Evaluation
Claim: org-authored MCP results are redacted with provenance; computed results unchanged
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
